div.head: Ps Cn for 24
div.ab: Sed si regalem feram, quam Angli a staggon appellant, alteruter coegerit anhelare, alter per unum annum, alter per duos careat libertate naturali; si uero seruus, pro utlagato habeatur, quem Angli frendlæsman uocant.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 624 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: But if either of them makes a royal beast, which the English call a staggon (a stag), pant, the one shall lose his natural freedom for one year, the other for two; but if a slave, let him be held an outlaw, whom the English call frendlæsman (friendless man).
